146	//  Swizzle mode (PTX ISA §<ip>.4, descriptor bits 62-61 "swizzle mode").
147	//
148	//  The shared-memory matrix descriptor encodes how the 128-bit core-matrix
149	//  rows are interleaved in smem to avoid bank conflicts on the wgmma read.
150	//  CRITICAL: the descriptor's layout_type field (bits 63:62) does NOT use a
151	//  size-ascending encoding. The hardware/CUTLASS encoding is
152	//  (cute/arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp LayoutType, verified):
153	//    NONE/INTERLEAVE = 0,  SWIZZLE_128B = 1,  SWIZZLE_64B = 2,  SWIZZLE_32B = 3.
154	//  (An earlier draft had 32B=1/128B=3 swapped; the correctness path uses NONE=0
155	//  so it was unaffected, but the perf-phase swizzle modes MUST use these values.)
156	//
157	//  CORRECTNESS-PATH NOTE (deviation flagged in the report): the gated /
158	//  tested numerics path ships swizzle = NONE (kSwizzleNone). NONE is a
159	//  fully-legal descriptor mode (§<ip>.4) and is the layout the
160	//  correctness gates validate against torch. The 128B-swizzle layout is a
161	//  PERF-PHASE optimization (bank-conflict elimination on the smem read) and
162	//  is exposed here as the template parameter the model headers will select
163	//  once the quiet-GPU perf phase measures it; it is NOT required for any
164	//  correctness gate. See DESIGN §4.1 ("specify the 128-byte-swizzle layout"
165	//  is the perf target; phase-1 staging uses cp.async, §4.1 item 3).
166	// =========================================================================
167	enum SwizzleMode : uint32_t {
168	    kSwizzleNone = 0,   // INTERLEAVE / no swizzle (the correctness-path layout)
169	    kSwizzle128B = 1,   // SWIZZLE_128B
170	    kSwizzle64B  = 2,   // SWIZZLE_64B
171	    kSwizzle32B  = 3,   // SWIZZLE_32B
172	};

174	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
175	//  generic-smem-pointer → matrix-descriptor start address.
176	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.4: the descriptor's bits 13-0 hold the start address of
177	//  the matrix in shared memory, encoded as the 18-bit smem byte address with
178	//  the low 4 bits dropped — i.e. addr_field = (smem_byte_addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4.
179	//  The low 4 bits MUST be zero (16-byte alignment) or they are silently lost.
180	// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
181	__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_desc_encode_addr(const void* smem_ptr) {
182	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
183	    uint32_t a = static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(smem_ptr));
184	    return (a & 0x3FFFFu) >> 4;
185	#else
186	    (void)smem_ptr;
187	    return 0u;
188	#endif
189	}

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Shared-memory matrix descriptor (PTX ISA §<ip>.4).
193	//
194	//  64-bit layout (bit ranges per the ISA table):
195	//    bits  13: 0  start address (smem byte addr >> 4)
196	//    bits  15:14  (reserved / 0)
197	//    bits  29:16  leading-dimension byte offset (LBO) >> 4
198	//    bits  31:30  (reserved / 0)
199	//    bits  45:32  stride-dimension byte offset (SBO) >> 4
200	//    bits  48:46  (reserved / 0)
201	//    bits  51:49  matrix base offset (for swizzle; 0 for our tiles)
202	//    bits  61:52  (reserved / 0)
203	//    bits  63:62  swizzle / layout mode (0 none / 1 128B / 2 64B / 3 32B —
204	//                 the CUTLASS LayoutType encoding, see SwizzleMode above)
205	//
206	//  LBO and SBO are the byte offsets between consecutive "core matrices" along
207	//  the leading and stride dimensions respectively (§<ip>.3 "Strides").
208	//  Both are encoded >>4 (16-byte granular). The exact (LBO,SBO) depend on the
209	//  operand's smem tile layout; the make_desc_*_kmajor builders below compute
210	//  them for the canonical row-major-K bf16 tiles the model headers stage.
211	// =========================================================================
212	struct SmemDesc {
213	    uint64_t desc;
214	};
215	
216	// Low-level builder: caller supplies LBO/SBO in BYTES; we apply the >>4 and
217	// the swizzle field. Use the make_desc_*_kmajor convenience wrappers unless
218	// you have a bespoke smem layout.
219	template <SwizzleMode Swizzle = kSwizzleNone>
220	__device__ __forceinline__ SmemDesc make_smem_desc(
221	    const void* smem_base, uint32_t lbo_bytes, uint32_t sbo_bytes,
222	    uint32_t base_offset = 0u
223	) {
224	    SmemDesc d;
225	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
226	    uint64_t addr = static_cast<uint64_t>(smem_desc_encode_addr(smem_base));
227	    uint64_t lbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((lbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
228	    uint64_t sbo  = static_cast<uint64_t>((sbo_bytes >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);
229	    uint64_t bo   = static_cast<uint64_t>(base_offset & 0x7u);
230	    uint64_t sw   = static_cast<uint64_t>(Swizzle & 0x3u);
231	    d.desc = (addr)                 // bits 13:0
232	           | (lbo << 16)            // bits 29:16
233	           | (sbo << 32)            // bits 45:32
234	           | (bo  << 49)            // bits 51:49
235	           | (sw  << 62);           // bits 63:62
236	#else
237	    (void)smem_base; (void)lbo_bytes; (void)sbo_bytes; (void)base_offset;
238	    d.desc = 0;
239	#endif
240	    return d;
241	}

245	//  tiles the model headers stage (DESIGN §4.3: A tile 64×16 bf16, B tile
246	//  N×16 bf16). Major-K means the contraction dimension K is the operand's
247	//  inner GEMM dim and the wgmma reads the standard "TN" product
248	//  D[m,n] = Σ_k A[m,k]·B[n,k] with BOTH operands K-major (TransA=TransB=0).

250	//  REQUIRED smem layout (the CUTLASS-canonical Major-K INTERLEAVE layout —
251	//  ground truth, NOT a plain row-major block; see the report's "deviation"
252	//  section). For an operand of MN rows × 16 K-cols of bf16, element (mn,k) is
253	//  at the bf16 index:
254	//      idx(mn,k) = (k/8)*(MN*8) + mn*8 + (k%8)
255	//  i.e. the K=16 dim is two stacked 8-wide "core matrices", each an MN×8
256	//  row-major block of 128-bit rows: core-matrix 0 (k 0..7) occupies the first
257	//  MN*8 bf16 (MN*16 bytes), core-matrix 1 (k 8..15) the next MN*16 bytes.
258	//  The staging loops in the model headers / self-test / tile_pipeline MUST
259	//  write the tile in THIS layout (make_desc_* assumes it).

262	//  derived from cute::make_gmma_desc<Major::K> and verified against the cute
263	//  Layout_K_INTER_Atom byte offsets (report §"descriptor"):
264	//      SBO (stride byte offset)  = 128                 (8 MN-rows × 16 B/row)
265	//      LBO (leading byte offset) = MN * 16             (one core-matrix block)
266	//  Both are passed in BYTES; make_smem_desc applies the mandated >>4.
267	//  make_smem_desc routes lbo_bytes→leading-offset field (bits 29:16) and
268	//  sbo_bytes→stride-offset field (bits 45:32), matching cute's assignment
269	//  (leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10 = MN*16, stride_byte_offset_ = 128).

291	//  fp32 accumulator fragment for an m64×N output tile.
292	//  PTX ISA §<ip>.3 "Register fragment for .f32 accumulators" (the
293	//  m64nNk16 wgmma writes its output across the 128 warpgroup threads).
294	//
295	//  Fragment layout (the ISA figure, decoded):
296	//    - 128 threads = 4 warps; the M=64 rows are split so that
297	//        warp w  (w in 0..3)  owns rows  [16*w .. 16*w+15],
298	//      and within a warp, lane L owns two row-groups:
299	//        row_hi = 16*w + (L/4)        (rows 0..7 of the warp's block)
300	//        row_lo = row_hi + 8          (rows 8..15)
301	//    - The N columns are held as N/2 fp32 registers per thread, in pairs:
302	//        register pair (2c, 2c+1) holds columns (col_base+0, col_base+1)
303	//        where col_base = (L%4)*2 + 8*(c/2_grouped)...  [the (col%8) + 8*(c>>1)
304	//      grouping of the ISA]. We expose the exact decode via frag_row()/
305	//      frag_col() so the epilogue (and the self-test) maps register i of
306	//      lane L (in warp w) to the (row,col) of the 64×N output it represents.
307	//
308	//  We store N/2 floats. c[2*g + p] is the p-th (p in {0,1}) of register-group
309	//  g (g in [0, N/4) for the "even/odd column pair" grouping). The helpers
310	//  frag_row(lane,i) / frag_col(lane,i) give the global (row,col) so a single
311	//  authoritative decode is shared by the epilogue store AND the gate's
312	//  reference comparison (no chance of a mismatched private decode).
313	// =========================================================================
314	template <int N>
315	struct WgmmaAccum {
316	    static_assert(N % 8 == 0, "wgmma N must be a multiple of 8");
317	    static constexpr int kRegs = N / 2;   // fp32 regs per thread
318	    float c[kRegs];
319	
320	    __device__ __forceinline__ void zero() {
321	        #pragma unroll
322	        for (int i = 0; i < kRegs; ++i) c[i] = 0.0f;
323	    }
324	};

326	// --- Authoritative fragment decode (PTX ISA §<ip>.3, .f32 accumulators) -
327	// For thread `tid_in_wg` in [0,128) and register index `i` in [0, N/2):
328	//   warp = tid_in_wg / 32 ; lane = tid_in_wg % 32.
329	//   The 64 M-rows are partitioned warp-major: rows [16*warp, 16*warp+16).
330	//   lane bits decode within the warp's 16-row × N block as in the ISA figure:
331	//     group g = i / 2 ; sub p = i % 2.
332	//     row = 16*warp + (lane / 4) + 8 * (g % 2 == 0 ? 0 : 0)   -- see below.
333	//
334	// The ISA C-fragment for .m64nNk16.f32 lays out each lane's N/2 elements as
335	// (over the row pair r0=lane/4, r1=r0+8) interleaved column pairs. The precise
336	// closed form, validated by the A=I gate, is:
337	//   group_of_8 = i / 8 ;   within = i % 8
338	//   row = 16*warp + (lane/4) + 8*(within / 4)
339	//   col = (lane%4)*2 + (within % 2) + 8*group_of_8 + ...
340	// To keep ONE source of truth that the gate verifies bit-for-bit, the decode
341	// is implemented below in the exact factored form the ISA figure gives for
342	// the 16x8 sub-blocks the f32 accumulator tiles across N.
343	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_frag_decode(
344	    int tid_in_wg, int i, int N, int& row, int& col
345	) {
346	    const int warp = tid_in_wg >> 5;       // 0..3
347	    const int lane = tid_in_wg & 31;       // 0..31
348	    // Each 16x8 output sub-block (one "n8" column slab) contributes 4 regs
349	    // per thread (8 rows split into 2 row-halves × ... ). The ISA's .f32
350	    // fragment for an n8 slab gives, per lane:
351	    //   reg 0 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
352	    //   reg 1 -> (row = lane/4,       col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
353	    //   reg 2 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 0)
354	    //   reg 3 -> (row = lane/4 + 8,   col = (lane%4)*2 + 1)
355	    // and successive n8 slabs add 8 to the column. With N columns there are
356	    // N/8 slabs × 4 regs = N/2 regs (matches kRegs).
357	    const int slab   = i >> 2;             // which n8 column slab (0..N/8-1)
358	    const int within = i & 3;              // 0..3 within the slab
359	    const int row_half = within >> 1;      // 0 -> rows 0..7, 1 -> rows 8..15
360	    const int col_par  = within & 1;       // 0 or 1 column within the pair
361	    row = 16 * warp + (lane >> 2) + 8 * row_half;
362	    col = (lane & 3) * 2 + col_par + 8 * slab;
363	    (void)N;
364	}

410	//    - `acc`  : the fp32 accumulator fragment (N/2 regs, inout). With
411	//               ScaleD=1 it is D = A*B + D (accumulate); ScaleD=0 is D = A*B

593	// =========================================================================
594	//  K-chain mainloop helper — the choreography in one call (the integration
595	//  seam the model headers invoke for a K-tile chain). DESIGN §3.1.
596	//
597	//  Runs `k_steps` ss-wgmma issues over a fixed ASCENDING k-order (the
598	//  determinism rule: one CTA owns the tile end-to-end, k ascending, no
599	//  work-steal split, no float atomics → bitwise-reproducible). The FIRST
600	//  issue uses ScaleD=0 (overwrite, so the accumulator need not be pre-zeroed
601	//  for a fresh tile); subsequent issues accumulate (ScaleD=1). One
602	//  wgmma_fence() before the group, one commit_group()+wait_group<0>() after.
603	//
604	//  `gen` is a functor: gen(k) -> {descA, descB} for k-step k (the caller
605	//  advances the smem base / pipeline stage between k-steps). Keeping the
606	//  descriptor generation a callback is what lets the SAME mainloop serve the
607	//  unpipelined gate (gen reads a fixed pre-staged tile array) and the
608	//  pipelined gate (gen reads the current ring-buffer stage) with bit-identical
609	//  numerics — the property gate (c) checks.
610	//
611	//  NOTE on fence placement: when the caller has pre-written the accumulator
612	//  with non-wgmma code (zero(), or a partial from a previous chain it wants to
613	//  ACCUMULATE onto), it must call wgmma_fence() itself and pass
614	//  FenceBeforeFirst=false + start with ScaleD=1. The default
615	//  (FenceBeforeFirst=true, first issue ScaleD=0) is the fresh-tile case.
616	// =========================================================================
617	template <int N, int TransA, int TransB, bool FenceBeforeFirst = true,
618	          typename DescGen>
619	__device__ __forceinline__ void wgmma_mainloop_kchain(
620	    WgmmaAccum<N>& acc, int k_steps, DescGen gen
621	) {
622	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
623	    if (FenceBeforeFirst) wgmma_fence();
624	    // First k-step OVERWRITES (ScaleD=0) so a fresh accumulator is correct
625	    // without a separate zero. (If the caller wants to accumulate onto a
626	    // pre-existing fp32 value, it sets FenceBeforeFirst=false, zeroes/sets the
627	    // accumulator + fences itself, and we still issue k=0 below — but then the
628	    // caller should pass an accumulating first step; for the common fresh-tile
629	    // path this is exactly D = sum_k A_k B_k.)
630	    {
631	        auto d = gen(0);
632	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
633	    }
634	    #pragma unroll 1
635	    for (int k = 1; k < k_steps; ++k) {
636	        auto d = gen(k);
637	        wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, TransA, TransB>(acc, d.first, d.second);
638	    }
639	    wgmma_commit_group();
640	    wgmma_wait_group<0>();
641	#else
642	    (void)acc; (void)k_steps; (void)gen;
643	#endif
644	}

76	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
77	//
78	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
79	//  Every CTA runs:
80	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
81	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
82	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
83	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
84	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
85	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
86	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
87	//
88	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
89	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
90	// =========================================================================
91	struct TaskQueue {
92	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
93	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
94	
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
96	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
97	
98	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
99	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
100	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
102	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
103	    }
104	
105	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
106	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
107	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
108	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
109	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
110	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
111	        }
112	        __syncthreads();
113	        int t = *smem_slot;
114	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
115	        return t;
116	    }
117	};

119	// =========================================================================
120	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
121	//
122	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
123	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
124	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
125	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
126	//
127	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
128	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
129	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
135	//
136	//  Fences (§1.14):
137	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
141	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
142	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
143	//
144	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
146	// =========================================================================
147	struct GridBarrier {
148	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
149	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
150	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
151	
152	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
153	                                            unsigned* generation,
154	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
155	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
156	
157	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
158	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
159	        __syncthreads();
160	
161	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
162	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
163	            unsigned my_gen =
164	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
165	
166	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
167	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
168	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
169	            __threadfence();
170	
171	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
172	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
173	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
174	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
175	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
176	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
179	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
180	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
181	                __threadfence();
182	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
183	            } else {
184	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
185	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
186	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
187	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
188	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
189	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
190	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
191	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
192	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
193	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
194	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
195	                       == my_gen) {
196	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
197	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
198	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
199	#endif
200	                }
201	            }
202	
203	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
204	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
205	            __threadfence();
206	        }
207	
208	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
209	        __syncthreads();
210	    }

212	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
213	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
214	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
215	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
216	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
217	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
218	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
219	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
220	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
221	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
222	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
223	        __syncthreads();
224	
225	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
226	            unsigned my_gen =
227	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
228	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
229	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
230	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
231	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
232	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
233	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
234	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
235	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
236	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
237	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
238	                __threadfence();
239	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
240	            } else {
241	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
242	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
243	                       == my_gen) {
244	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
245	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
246	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
247	#endif
248	                }
249	            }
250	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
251	        }
252	
253	        __syncthreads();
254	    }
255	};

258	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
259	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
260	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
261	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.
262	// =========================================================================
263	struct PersistentContext {
264	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
265	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
266	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
267	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
268	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
269	
270	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
271	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
272	    }
273	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
274	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
275	    }
276	};

100	//  Ring-buffer geometry for one (A 64×16 + B N×16) bf16 stage.
101	//  A tile: 64×16 bf16 = 2048 B.  B tile: N×16 bf16 = N*32 B.
102	//  All tiles K-contiguous (row-major), matching make_desc_{A,B}_kmajor.
103	// =========================================================================
104	template <int N>
105	struct TileGeom {
106	    static constexpr int kAElems   = 64 * kWgmmaAtomK;        // 1024
107	    static constexpr int kBElems   = N  * kWgmmaAtomK;        // N*16
108	    static constexpr int kABytes   = kAElems * (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);
109	    static constexpr int kBBytes   = kBElems * (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);
110	    static constexpr int kStageBytes = kABytes + kBBytes;
111	    static constexpr uint32_t kARowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
112	    static constexpr uint32_t kBRowStride = kWgmmaAtomK * (uint32_t)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16); // 32
113	    // tx-bytes for the stage's two cp.async transactions (full barrier expects).
114	    static constexpr int kStageTxBytes = kStageBytes;

118	//  TilePipeline — the Depth-stage ring + its mbarriers.
119	//
120	//  smem layout the caller hands us (one contiguous arena, 16B-aligned):
121	//    [ stage0 A | stage0 B | stage1 A | stage1 B | ... | full[Depth] | empty[Depth] ]
122	//  where each stage's A is 16B-aligned (kAElems is a multiple of 8 bf16 = 16B)
123	//  and B follows (also 16B-multiple for the design's N). The two mbarrier
124	//  arrays are 8-byte words.
125	//
126	//  Two barriers per stage (the canonical producer/consumer ring):
127	//    full[s]  : producer arrives (expect_tx) when it has issued the loads for
128	//               stage s; consumer waits on it before issuing wgmma.
129	//    empty[s] : consumer arrives when it has finished consuming stage s;
130	//               producer waits on it before overwriting stage s (so the
131	//               in-flight wgmma is not clobbered). For Depth-buffering the
132	//               producer can run Depth stages ahead before it must wait.
133	//
134	//  Phase parity: each barrier flips parity every time its expected arrivals

136	// =========================================================================
137	//  NOTE on storage: Mbarrier (warp_specialize.cuh) is a thin wrapper around a

141	//  on-demand via full(s) / empty(s) — a zero-cost wrapper around the word.
142	template <int N, int Depth>
143	struct TilePipeline {
144	    __nv_bfloat16* ring;          // [Depth] × (A|B) tiles, 16B-aligned
145	    unsigned long long* bars;     // [2*Depth] mbarrier words: full[Depth] then empty[Depth]
146	
147	    // Construct over a caller-provided smem arena. `arena` points at the start
148	    // of the ring (must be 16B-aligned). The barrier words follow the tiles.
149	    __device__ __forceinline__ TilePipeline(void* arena)
150	        : ring(reinterpret_cast<__nv_bfloat16*>(arena)),
151	          bars(reinterpret_cast<unsigned long long*>(
152	              reinterpret_cast<char*>(arena) +
153	              (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes)) {}
154	
155	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier full(int s)  { return Mbarrier(bars + s); }
156	    __device__ __forceinline__ Mbarrier empty(int s) { return Mbarrier(bars + Depth + s); }
157	
158	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageA(int s) {
159	        return ring + (size_t)s * (TileGeom<N>::kAElems + TileGeom<N>::kBElems);
160	    }
161	    __device__ __forceinline__ __nv_bfloat16* stageB(int s) {
162	        return stageA(s) + TileGeom<N>::kAElems;
163	    }
164	
165	    // Bytes the caller must allocate as dynamic smem for this pipeline.
166	    static constexpr size_t smem_bytes() {
167	        return (size_t)Depth * TileGeom<N>::kStageBytes +
168	               (size_t)2 * Depth * sizeof(unsigned long long);
169	    }

171	    // Init the barriers (one thread of the block). Each barrier expects a FULL
172	    // WARPGROUP (128) of arrivals per phase: full[] is arrived by all 128
173	    // producer threads (so the phase-flip happens-after every thread's
174	    // cp.async + wait_group, giving the consumer a warpgroup-wide visibility
175	    // guarantee), empty[] by all 128 consumer threads. (An earlier draft used
176	    // init(1) + a per-warp elect_one_sync arrive — but elect.sync elects one
177	    // leader PER WARP, so 4 warps produced 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier,
178	    // flipping the phase an even number of times and DEADLOCKING the consumer's
179	    // try_wait.parity. count=128 + all-threads-arrive is the correct contract.)
180	    __device__ __forceinline__ void init_barriers() {
181	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
182	            #pragma unroll
183	            for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) {
184	                full(s).init(128);
185	                empty(s).init(128);

187	        }
188	    }

191	// =========================================================================
192	//  Producer-side staging of ONE K-tile (stage `slot`, k-index `k`) via
193	//  cp.async (DESIGN §4.2 WG0). Issues 16-byte cp.async copies of the A and B
194	//  tiles from HBM into the ring slot, then the elected leader does
195	//  arrive_expect_tx(tx) on the stage's `full` barrier so the consumer knows
196	//  the bytes are inbound. cp.async + mbarrier transaction-count is the
197	//  standard Hopper async-load handshake.
198	//
199	//  NOTE: this uses cp.async (.cg.16), NOT TMA — DESIGN §4.1 item 3 makes TMA
200	//  explicitly phase-2; phase-1 staging is cp.async (already overlaps load
201	//  latency). For cp.async the transaction completion is signalled via
202	//  cp.async.mbarrier.arrive (the bytes are counted by the barrier). We model
203	//  that with arrive_expect_tx on the producer leader + cp_async_commit, and
204	//  the consumer's try_wait/parity gates on it.
205	// =========================================================================
206	template <int N, int Depth>
207	__device__ __forceinline__ void pipeline_produce_ktile(
208	    TilePipeline<N, Depth>& pipe, int slot, int k,
209	    const __nv_bfloat16* gA, const __nv_bfloat16* gB, int /*k_steps*/
210	) {
211	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
212	    const int wtid = threadIdx.x & 127;          // 0..127 within WG0
213	    __nv_bfloat16* dA = pipe.stageA(slot);
214	    __nv_bfloat16* dB = pipe.stageB(slot);
215	    const __nv_bfloat16* sA = gA + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kAElems;  // row-major MxK
216	    const __nv_bfloat16* sB = gB + (size_t)k * TileGeom<N>::kBElems;  // row-major NxK
217	
218	    // 16B (8 bf16) cp.async copies SCATTERED into the canonical Major-K layout
219	    // (two stacked 8-wide core matrices) make_desc_*_kmajor requires. A global
220	    // row (mn, 0..15) splits into two 16B halves: half 0 (k 0..7) lands at
221	    // mn*8, half 1 (k 8..15) at MN*8 + mn*8 — both 16B-aligned. kVec=8 bf16.
222	    constexpr int kVec = 16 / (int)sizeof(__nv_bfloat16);   // 8 bf16 / 16B
223	    // A: MN=64. 64 rows × 2 halves = 128 vectors.
224	    constexpr int kAHalves = 64 * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);     // 64*2 = 128
225	    for (int v = wtid; v < kAHalves; v += 128) {
226	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..63
227	        const int half = v & 1;                 // 0 or 1
228	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sA + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
229	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dA + (size_t)half * (64 * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
230	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
231	    }
232	    // B: MN=N. N rows × 2 halves vectors.
233	    constexpr int kBHalves = N * (kWgmmaAtomK / kVec);      // N*2
234	    for (int v = wtid; v < kBHalves; v += 128) {
235	        const int mn = v >> 1;                  // 0..N-1
236	        const int half = v & 1;
237	        const __nv_bfloat16* src = sB + (size_t)mn * kWgmmaAtomK + (size_t)half * kVec;
238	        __nv_bfloat16* dst = dB + (size_t)half * (N * kVec) + (size_t)mn * kVec;
239	        prim::cp_async_cg_16(dst, src);
240	    }
241	    prim::cp_async_commit();
242	    // Drain THIS stage's group before signalling full, so the consumer's wgmma
243	    // (which reads smem directly, not through the mbarrier transaction count)
244	    // sees landed bytes. cp.async.wait_group<0> + the arrive gives a correct
245	    // handshake without relying on cp.async.mbarrier.arrive byte-counting
246	    // (which would require the .mbarrier.arrive variant; we keep the portable
247	    // wait_group form from primitives.cuh and use the mbarrier purely as the
248	    // cross-warpgroup ready signal). DESIGN §4.2: one async-proxy fence per
249	    // hand-off.
250	    prim::cp_async_wait_group<0>();
251	    fence_async_proxy();
252	    // ALL 128 producer threads arrive (barrier count=128). Each thread's
253	    // arrive happens-after its own cp.async + wait_group<0>, so the phase-flip
254	    // (on the 128th arrive) is visibility-ordered after every staged byte.
255	    pipe.full(slot).arrive();       // signal: stage `slot` is ready to consume
256	#else
257	    (void)pipe; (void)slot; (void)k; (void)gA; (void)gB;
258	#endif
259	}

261	// =========================================================================
262	//  tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16 — the turnkey single-CTA pipelined GEMM.
263	//  blockDim.x = 256: WG0 = producer (tid 0..127), WG1 = consumer (128..255).
264	//  DESIGN §4.2 producer/consumer structure, §4.3 occupancy budget.
265	//
266	//  Determinism: the consumer issues wgmma in ASCENDING k (fixed order); the
267	//  pipeline only changes operand-availability timing, not the reduction order,
268	//  so the fp32 accumulation is bit-identical to the unpipelined kchain
269	//  (DESIGN gate c).
270	// =========================================================================
271	template <int N, int Depth>
272	__device__ __forceinline__ void tc_pipelined_gemm_m64nNk16(
273	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gA,
274	    const __nv_bfloat16* __restrict__ gB,
275	    float* __restrict__ gD, int k_steps
276	) {
277	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
278	    extern __shared__ char smem_raw[];
279	    // 16B-align the ring arena.
280	    uintptr_t base = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(smem_raw);
281	    uintptr_t aligned = (base + 15u) & ~uintptr_t(15u);
282	    TilePipeline<N, Depth> pipe(reinterpret_cast<void*>(aligned));
283	    pipe.init_barriers();
284	    __syncthreads();
285	
286	    const int warpgroup = threadIdx.x / 128;    // 0 = producer, 1 = consumer
287	    const bool is_producer = (warpgroup == 0);
288	
289	    // Register rebalance (DESIGN §4.2): producer few regs, consumer many.
290	    // Guarded by SG_TUNED_*_REGS != 0 (0 disables for portability/debug).
291	#if (SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS != 0) && (SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS != 0)
292	    if (is_producer) warpgroup_reg_dealloc<SG_TUNED_PROD_REGS>();
293	    else             warpgroup_reg_alloc  <SG_TUNED_CONS_REGS>();
294	#endif
295	
296	    if (is_producer) {
297	        // Producer: stage every K-tile in ascending k. With Depth buffering it
298	        // may run up to Depth stages ahead; we gate reuse of a slot on the
299	        // consumer having released it (empty[slot]).
300	        unsigned empty_parity[Depth];
301	        #pragma unroll
302	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) empty_parity[s] = 0u;
303	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
304	            const int slot = k % Depth;
305	            // For k >= Depth, the slot was used by k-Depth; wait until the
306	            // consumer released it (empty barrier) before overwriting.
307	            if (k >= Depth) {
308	                pipe.empty(slot).wait(empty_parity[slot]);
309	                empty_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
310	            }
311	            pipeline_produce_ktile<N, Depth>(pipe, slot, k, gA, gB, k_steps);
312	        }
313	    } else {
314	        // Consumer: wgmma over each staged K-tile in ascending k. The fp32
315	        // fragment accumulates across the whole chain (first k overwrites).
316	        WgmmaAccum<N> acc;
317	        unsigned full_parity[Depth];
318	        #pragma unroll
319	        for (int s = 0; s < Depth; ++s) full_parity[s] = 0u;
320	
321	        // We can't use the kchain helper directly (it expects all descriptors
322	        // available); instead we inline the SAME choreography: one fence, then
323	        // k=0 overwrite / k>0 accumulate, commit+wait at the end. Issuing each
324	        // wgmma right after its stage is ready overlaps load and compute.
325	        wgmma_fence();
326	        for (int k = 0; k < k_steps; ++k) {
327	            const int slot = k % Depth;
328	            pipe.full(slot).wait(full_parity[slot]);
329	            full_parity[slot] ^= 1u;
330	
331	            __nv_bfloat16* aTile = pipe.stageA(slot);
332	            __nv_bfloat16* bTile = pipe.stageB(slot);
333	            SmemDesc dA = make_desc_A_kmajor</*M=*/64, kSwizzleNone>(aTile);
334	            SmemDesc dB = make_desc_B_kmajor</*N=*/N,  kSwizzleNone>(bTile);
335	            // Both operands Major-K ⇒ TransA=0, TransB=0 (cute Major::K == 0).
336	            if (k == 0) {
337	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/0, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
338	            } else {
339	                wgmma_m64nNk16_bf16<N, /*ScaleD=*/1, /*TransA=*/0, /*TransB=*/0>(acc, dA, dB);
340	            }
341	            // Commit + wait THIS issue before releasing the slot, so the
342	            // producer does not overwrite operands the async wgmma still reads.
343	            wgmma_commit_group();
344	            wgmma_wait_group<0>();
345	            // Release the slot back to the producer. ALL 128 consumer threads
346	            // arrive (barrier count=128) — see init_barriers: the per-warp elect
347	            // would give 4 arrivals on a count-1 barrier and deadlock.
348	            pipe.empty(slot).arrive();
349	        }
350	
351	        // Epilogue: store the fp32 fragment. The consumer warpgroup owns the
352	        // output; decode relative to its 128-thread group (tid-128).
353	        const int tid_in_wg = threadIdx.x - 128;
354	        #pragma unroll
355	        for (int i = 0; i < WgmmaAccum<N>::kRegs; ++i) {

4	// §3.4 / §4.5 — Hopper warp-specialization primitives.
5	//
6	// These are the building blocks the Stage-6 L3 persistent megakernel composes
7	// for its producer/consumer (load / compute) warp-group split:
8	//
9	//   * elect_one_sync      — single-leader election within a warp (the lane that
10	//                           issues TMA / cp.async.bulk on behalf of the group),
11	//                           via the `elect.sync` instruction (1 instr vs a
12	//                           ballot+ffs).
13	//   * Mbarrier            — shared-memory async transaction barrier
14	//                           (`mbarrier.*`), used to signal load→compute handoff
15	//                           with arrive/expect-tx and try_wait/parity.
16	//   * warpgroup_reg_alloc/dealloc — `setmaxnreg.{inc,dec}` register
17	//                           reallocation between the producer (few regs) and
18	//                           consumer (many regs) warp-groups.
19	//
20	// All are sm_90+ and guarded; on older arches the helpers degrade to a correct
21	// (if unspecialized) fallback so the codegen matrix still builds. Fence usage
22	// is kept explicit and minimal — loose `fence.proxy.async` placement is a known
23	// >10% perf footgun (ThunderKittens), so callers pair an mbarrier handoff with
24	// exactly one async-proxy fence, documented at each call site in Stage 6.
25	//
26	// NOTE: this header defines PRIMITIVES only — it is composed by the megakernel
27	// (Stage 6). It is intentionally NOT retrofitted into the elementwise optimizer
28	// kernels, where a producer/consumer split would be a no-op.
29	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

31	#include "csrc/common/platform.h"
32	#include <cuda_runtime.h>

34	namespace sg { namespace sm90 { namespace wgs {

36	// =========================================================================
37	//  elect.sync — elect a single leader lane among `membermask` (default: the
38	//  full warp). Returns true on exactly one lane. On pre-sm_90, falls back to
39	//  ballot + find-first-set (lane == lowest active lane).
40	// =========================================================================
41	__device__ __forceinline__ bool elect_one_sync(unsigned membermask = 0xffffffffu) {
42	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
43	    unsigned pred;
44	    asm volatile(
45	        "{\n\t"
46	        ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
47	        "elect.sync _|p, %1;\n\t"
48	        "selp.u32 %0, 1, 0, p;\n\t"
49	        "}\n\t"
50	        : "=r"(pred) : "r"(membermask));
51	    return pred != 0u;
52	#else
53	    unsigned active = __ballot_sync(membermask, 1);
54	    int leader = __ffs(active) - 1;
55	    return (threadIdx.x & 31) == leader;
56	#endif
57	}
58	
59	// =========================================================================
60	//  Mbarrier — shared-memory async transaction barrier (mbarrier.*).
61	//
62	//  Producer/consumer handoff protocol (Stage-6 megakernel):
63	//    init(expected_arrivals)             // once, by one thread
64	//    producer: arrive_expect_tx(bytes)   // announce an incoming TMA/cp.async
65	//              <issue TMA / cp.async.bulk into shared>
66	//    consumer: while(!try_wait(parity)){} // spin until the transaction lands
67	//              <read shared>
68	//    flip parity each phase.
69	//
70	//  The barrier object is a single 8-byte shared word the caller owns.
71	// =========================================================================
72	struct Mbarrier {
73	    unsigned long long* addr;  // shared-memory barrier state (8 bytes)
74	
75	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit Mbarrier(unsigned long long* shared_word)
76	        : addr(shared_word) {}
77	
78	    __device__ __forceinline__ unsigned smem_u32() const {
79	        return static_cast<unsigned>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(addr));
80	    }
81	
82	    __device__ __forceinline__ void init(int expected_arrivals) const {
83	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
84	        asm volatile("mbarrier.init.shared.b64 [%0], %1;"
85	                     :: "r"(smem_u32()), "r"(expected_arrivals));
86	#else
87	        (void)expected_arrivals;
88	#endif
89	    }
90	
91	    __device__ __forceinline__ void invalidate() const {
92	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
93	        asm volatile("mbarrier.inval.shared.b64 [%0];" :: "r"(smem_u32()));
94	#endif
95	    }
96	
97	    // Producer: arrive AND declare `tx_bytes` of pending async transactions.
98	    __device__ __forceinline__ void arrive_expect_tx(int tx_bytes) const {
99	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
100	        asm volatile(
101	            "mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.shared.b64 _, [%0], %1;"
102	            :: "r"(smem_u32()), "r"(tx_bytes));
103	#else
104	        (void)tx_bytes;
105	#endif
106	    }
107	
108	    // Plain arrive (no transaction bytes).
109	    __device__ __forceinline__ void arrive() const {
110	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
111	        asm volatile("mbarrier.arrive.shared.b64 _, [%0];" :: "r"(smem_u32()));
112	#endif
113	    }
114	
115	    // Consumer: non-blocking test for the given phase parity. Returns true once
116	    // the expected arrivals + transaction bytes for this phase have completed.
117	    __device__ __forceinline__ bool try_wait(unsigned phase_parity) const {
118	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
119	        unsigned done;
120	        asm volatile(
121	            "{\n\t"
122	            ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
123	            "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared.b64 p, [%1], %2;\n\t"
124	            "selp.u32 %0, 1, 0, p;\n\t"
125	            "}\n\t"
126	            : "=r"(done) : "r"(smem_u32()), "r"(phase_parity));
127	        return done != 0u;
128	#else
129	        (void)phase_parity;
130	        return true;  // unspecialized fallback: no async transactions in flight
131	#endif
132	    }
133	
134	    // Blocking wait (spin) for the phase.
135	    __device__ __forceinline__ void wait(unsigned phase_parity) const {
136	        while (!try_wait(phase_parity)) { /* spin */ }
137	    }
138	};

140	// One async-proxy fence, paired with an mbarrier handoff. Kept as a named
141	// helper so Stage-6 call sites issue EXACTLY ONE (loose placement is a >10%
142	// regression). Orders generic-proxy writes before async-proxy (TMA) consumers.
143	__device__ __forceinline__ void fence_async_proxy() {
144	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
145	    asm volatile("fence.proxy.async.shared::cta;");
146	#endif

150	//  setmaxnreg — warp-group register reallocation (Hopper). The producer
151	//  (TMA-issuing) warp-group deallocates down to N; the consumer (WGMMA)
152	//  warp-group allocates up to N. Must be called uniformly by all warps in
153	//  the warp-group, and only in a kernel launched with the matching
154	//  __launch_bounds__/cluster config (Stage 6 sets that up).
155	//
156	//  N is a template parameter: setmaxnreg requires a compile-time-constant
157	//  register count (PTX immediate operand).
158	// =========================================================================
159	template <int N>
160	__device__ __forceinline__ void warpgroup_reg_dealloc() {
161	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
162	    asm volatile("setmaxnreg.dec.sync.aligned.u32 %0;" :: "n"(N));
163	#endif
164	}
165	
166	template <int N>
167	__device__ __forceinline__ void warpgroup_reg_alloc() {
168	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900)
169	    asm volatile("setmaxnreg.inc.sync.aligned.u32 %0;" :: "n"(N));
170	#endif
171	}

427	        a.X_ctx[li]  = p + off; off += Td;

429	        a.X_gact[li] = p + off; off += Tff;

442	//  bf16 WEIGHT PRE-STAGE (reg-pressure campaign C1 + cp.async-ring blocker (a)).
443	//  The fwd/dX GEMMs' B operand was the fp32 params blob CONVERTED ON READ
444	//  (__float2bfloat16 inside the staging accessor). That conversion web is the
445	//  measured marginal register demand of the K-loop (the pure-bf16 dW path
446	//  allocates spill-free at the same accumulator width while the fp32-read
447	//  fwd/dX paths spill ~2.2 KB when isolated), and it is the documented blocker
448	//  (a) of the cp.async/TMA ring: an async copy cannot convert, so the dominant
449	//  operand could not stream. Fix: convert ONCE per step into a bf16 weight
450	//  cache carved from the workspace, and stage the GEMM B operand from the
451	//  cache. cache[i] = __float2bfloat16(params[i]) is the IDENTICAL deterministic
452	//  per-element rounding the on-read path performed -> every GEMM consumes
453	//  BIT-IDENTICAL operand values; numerics/parity/A-A-A are unchanged BY
454	//  CONSTRUCTION (pure caching of a pure function; no reorder, no reassociation).
455	//
456	//  Only the 8 per-layer GEMM weight matrices (in_w/out_w/ff0_w/ff2_w x layers)
457	//  are cached: they are the ONLY fp32->bf16 on-read GEMM operands (the head
458	//  runs scalar fp32 per the oracle; embeddings/biases/LN are scalar fp32; the
459	//  dW GEMM operands are bf16 acts already). All sizes derive from the layout
460	//  constants -- no problem-specific hardcoding; the bench layout scales it.
461	//
462	//  C1-T (RING): a SECOND section of the cache holds the same 8 matrices
463	//  TRANSPOSED (W^T [Kin,Nout]). The dX GEMM reads W transposed; from the
464	//  row-major cache that staging is a k-stride 2-byte gather, which no 4/8/16B
465	//  cp.async can express (the same structural shape as ring blocker (b)).
466	//  Staging dX's B operand from W^T instead makes its tile rows K-CONTIGUOUS,
467	//  so the cp.async double-buffered ring streams BOTH fwd and dX weight
468	//  operands. WT[r,c] == W-cache[c,r] bit-identically (same fp32 element, same
469	//  deterministic rounding, written by exactly one thread) -> operand values,
470	//  parity and A/A/A are unchanged by construction. Cost: the cache doubles
471	//  (1.57 MB at d=128, 101 MB at d=1024 -- workspace headroom verified at both).
472	// ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
473	struct DecWBf {
474	    const __nv_bfloat16* in_w[dec::kLayers];    // [3d, d]  per layer
475	    const __nv_bfloat16* out_w[dec::kLayers];   // [d, d]   per layer
476	    const __nv_bfloat16* ff0_w[dec::kLayers];   // [dff, d] per layer
477	    const __nv_bfloat16* ff2_w[dec::kLayers];   // [d, dff] per layer
478	    // ── C1-T (RING section): the SAME four matrices stored TRANSPOSED, W^T
479	    //    [Kin, Nout] row-major. WT[r,c] == W-cache[c,r] BIT-IDENTICAL (the same
480	    //    __float2bfloat16 of the same fp32 element, stored twice). Purpose: the
481	    //    dX GEMM's B operand reads W TRANSPOSED (srcB(n=kin,k=out) = W[out,kin],
482	    //    a k-stride-Kin 2-byte gather the cp.async ring cannot stream — the same
483	    //    structural shape as ring blocker (b)). Staging from W^T instead makes
484	    //    the dX B-tile rows K-CONTIGUOUS (16B-chunkable), unblocking the ring on
485	    //    the dX path with UNCHANGED operand values → numerics/parity/A-A-A
486	    //    identical by construction. ──
487	    const __nv_bfloat16* in_wT[dec::kLayers];   // [d, 3d]  per layer
488	    const __nv_bfloat16* out_wT[dec::kLayers];  // [d, d]   per layer
489	    const __nv_bfloat16* ff0_wT[dec::kLayers];  // [d, dff] per layer
490	    const __nv_bfloat16* ff2_wT[dec::kLayers];  // [dff, d] per layer
491	};
492	constexpr int64_t kWbfInW        = (int64_t)3 * dec::kD * dec::kD;
493	constexpr int64_t kWbfOutW       = (int64_t)dec::kD * dec::kD;
494	constexpr int64_t kWbfFf0W       = (int64_t)dec::kDff * dec::kD;
495	constexpr int64_t kWbfFf2W       = (int64_t)dec::kD * dec::kDff;
496	constexpr int64_t kWbfLayerElems = kWbfInW + kWbfOutW + kWbfFf0W + kWbfFf2W;
497	constexpr int64_t kWbfTotalElems = (int64_t)dec::kLayers * kWbfLayerElems;
498	// Full cache: straight section [kWbfTotalElems] + transposed section (C1-T,
499	// same element count — every matrix size is a multiple of 8 so both sections
500	// and every per-matrix base stay 16B-aligned for the cp.async ring).
501	constexpr int64_t kWbfCacheElems = 2 * kWbfTotalElems;
502	// Workspace floats the cache occupies (bf16 elems -> float units, rounded up).
503	__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ int64_t dec_wbf_floats() {
504	    return (kWbfCacheElems + 1) / 2;
505	}
506	__device__ __forceinline__ DecWBf dec_wbf_bind(const __nv_bfloat16* c) {
507	    DecWBf wb;
508	    #pragma unroll
509	    for (int li = 0; li < dec::kLayers; ++li) {
510	        const __nv_bfloat16* b = c + (int64_t)li * kWbfLayerElems;
511	        wb.in_w[li]  = b;
512	        wb.out_w[li] = b + kWbfInW;
513	        wb.ff0_w[li] = b + kWbfInW + kWbfOutW;
514	        wb.ff2_w[li] = b + kWbfInW + kWbfOutW + kWbfFf0W;
515	        // transposed section (C1-T): same per-layer/per-matrix offsets, based
516	        // kWbfTotalElems further in (element counts identical per matrix).
517	        const __nv_bfloat16* t = b + kWbfTotalElems;
518	        wb.in_wT[li]  = t;
519	        wb.out_wT[li] = t + kWbfInW;
520	        wb.ff0_wT[li] = t + kWbfInW + kWbfOutW;
521	        wb.ff2_wT[li] = t + kWbfInW + kWbfOutW + kWbfFf0W;
522	    }
523	    return wb;
524	}
525	// Grid-strided fp32->bf16 convert of the 8 matrices into the cache. Element-
526	// owned (each cache index written by exactly one thread), no atomics ->

# IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — replace the hand-rolled ss-wgmma engine with a CuTe device-atom GEMM

Target: the persistent decoder megakernel (`fused_decoder_megakernel_tc`). Replace
the inner per-tile GEMM (TMA load → swizzled smem → pipelined CuTe GMMA atoms in
ascending k → CuTe-fragment epilogue) while keeping 1-CTA/SM + the hand-built
`GridBarrier`, ascending-k fp32 determinism, and the fp64/A-A-A gate. Incremental,
gated, byte-identical when OFF. CPU-only synthesis — no compile/run here.

References use `file:line` into `/workspace/SuperGrok1.5`. CUTLASS = v3.6.0 at
`third_party/cutlass/include/`. Companion deep digest:
`/workspace/cute_plan/CUTE_GEMM_SYNTHESIS.md`.

---

## 0. GUIDING PRINCIPLES (read before touching code)

- **Reject the COLLECTIVE, adopt the ATOMS.** CUTLASS `CollectiveMma` /
  `PipelineTmaAsync` are host-launched / cluster-bound (sm90_pipeline.hpp:271-628 use
  `ClusterBarrier` + `cute::cluster_shape()`) and are REJECTED (consistent with
  wgmma.cuh:16-18). We use device-callable CuTe atoms: `SM90_TMA_LOAD::copy`,
  `MMA_64xNx16_F32BF16BF16_SS::fma`, `GMMA::Layout_K_*_Atom`, and the project's OWN
  single-CTA `Mbarrier` (warp_specialize.cuh:72-138).
- **Two flags.** `SG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE` selects engine: `0` = hand wgmma (default,
  byte-identical), `1` = CuTe atoms. `SG_TUNED_GEMM_TMA` (sub-flag, only meaningful
  when ENGINE=1): `0` = CuTe MMA atoms but keep cp.async staging (de-risks the MMA
  swap from the TMA swap), `1` = add TMA load. `SG_TUNED_GEMM_SWIZZLE`: `0` =
  Layout_K_INTER (no swizzle, byte-identical smem), `1` = Layout_K_SW128. Default all
  0 ⇒ shipped PTX unchanged.
- **Gate everything with the existing tests** (`tests/hw/test_decoder_tc.py`:
  `_TC_LOSS_REL=1e-4` :534; grad rel≤2e-2 :255; `test_determinism_bitwise` :233 via
  `torch.equal`). Plus `decoder_tc_selftest.cu` per-orientation micro-gates and a new
  `test_cute_gemm.py`.
- **One GEMM first** (decoder fwd `dectc_gemm_fwd<128>`), prove the full pipeline,
  THEN expand to dX, then dW (the dW=dYᵀ·X transposed-strided GEMM is the biggest TMA
  win — it is the path the current code calls "out of scope, needs TMA-with-
  transpose" at model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:782-783).

---

## 1. HOST-SIDE TMA DESCRIPTOR CREATION

### 1.1 Where the descriptors are built
New header `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/cute_tma_desc.h` (host + a tiny device decl):
```cpp
// HOST ONLY. Builds a CUtensorMap for a row-major [rows, K] bf16 operand whose
// K is the contraction axis (Major-K). One descriptor per (base ptr, rows, K).
#include <cute/tensor.hpp>
#include <cute/atom/copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp>
namespace sg { namespace sm90 { namespace cute_gemm {
struct TmaPlan { CUtensorMap desc; /*128B POD*/ };
// build with make_tma_copy(SM90_TMA_LOAD{}, gtensor, smem_layout, cta_tiler, Int<1>{})
// gtensor = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(bf16_base), make_layout(make_shape(rows,K), make_stride(K,1)))
// smem_layout = tile_to_shape(GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bf16>{}, Shape<Int<TILE_MN>,Int<16>>{})
// cta_tiler = Shape<Int<TILE_MN>, Int<16>>{}, Cluster_Size = Int<1>{}
// then plan.desc = tma.get_tma_descriptor();  // raw CUtensorMap to copy to device
}}}
```
- `make_tma_copy(...)` is `CUTE_HOST_RTC` (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1268-1302); call
  it on host. `Cluster_Size = Int<1>{}` ⇒ single-CTA descriptor (no multicast).
- Extract the raw `CUtensorMap` (copy_sm90_desc.hpp:257 `using TmaDescriptor =
  CUtensorMap`). It is a 128-byte POD; memcpy the descriptors into a device buffer
  (`cudaMalloc` + `cudaMemcpy`) so the kernel reads them from global. (Alternatively
  pass each as a `__grid_constant__ const CUtensorMap` kernel param, but the
  persistent megakernel signature is fixed/wrapped — global buffer is simpler and
  matches the existing pointer-only launcher boundary, launcher.cu:16-19.)
- **Which descriptors:** for the decoder fwd/dX the B operand is the C1/C1-T bf16
  weight cache (`DecWBf`, model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:473-524) and the A operand is the
  token-row bf16 acts (`DecActs`, 401-417). Build:
  - per-weight-matrix fwd descriptor over `DecWBf::{in_w,out_w,ff0_w,ff2_w}[L]`
    (rows=Nout, K=Kin),
  - per-weight-matrix dX descriptor over the transposed `*_wT[L]` (rows=Kin, K=Nout),
  - per-acts-region descriptors over `DecActs::X_*`/`dY_*` (rows=T, K=d/3d/dff).
  These are ≈ a few dozen `CUtensorMap`s. The bf16 cache + acts base pointers and
  shapes are RUNTIME (depend on T=B·kSeq, d), so the descriptors are rebuilt when B/d
  changes (cache them keyed on (base,rows,K), like the launcher already caches
  workspace, launcher.cu:55-71).

### 1.2 Passing them into the megakernel via PersistentContext
EDIT `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` (PersistentContext, 263-276): add a nullable
pointer to a device array of `CUtensorMap` + a count (or a small typed struct
`CuteTmaCtx* g_tma;`). Keep it a raw `void*`/POD pointer so the wrapped launcher
boundary (plain pointers, launcher.cu:16-19) is unchanged and OFF builds ignore it.
```cpp
struct PersistentContext {
  int* g_next_task; unsigned* g_arrived; unsigned* g_generation;
  int n_tasks; unsigned n_ctas;
  const void* g_tma_desc = nullptr;   // device CUtensorMap[]; null ⇒ engine OFF
  int n_tma_desc = 0;
  ... };
```
- The host launcher (`launch_fused_decoder_megakernel_tc`, megakernel:1512, and the
  wrapper `mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc`, launcher.cu:102) builds the descriptors
  (§1.1), uploads them, sets `ctx.g_tma_desc`. Under `SG_TUNED_GEMM_TMA==0` it leaves
  it null. The launcher's ≥1-CTA/SM cert (megakernel:1540-1545) is UNTOUCHED.

---

## 2. DEVICE-SIDE PER-TILE GEMM (the new engine)

New header `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/cute_gemm.cuh`, namespace
`sg::sm90::cute_gemm`. It provides a drop-in replacement for
`tc_gemm_block_unpipelined<N,MaxAtomsM,SrcA,SrcB,Out>` with the SAME signature shape
(so the orientation wrappers in model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh switch engines with a
`#if`, not a rewrite).

### 2.1 Static layout objects (compile-time, zero register cost)
```cpp
using namespace cute;
using Atom = SM90::GMMA::MMA_64x128x16_F32BF16BF16_SS;   // N=128 default
// no-swizzle smem layout == the hand idx(mn,k) layout (byte-identical):
using SmemLayoutA = decltype(tile_to_shape(GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bfloat16_t>{},
                                           Shape<_64, _16>{}));
using SmemLayoutB = decltype(tile_to_shape(GMMA::Layout_K_INTER_Atom<bfloat16_t>{},
                                           Shape<Int<N>, _16>{}));
// swizzle variant (behind SG_TUNED_GEMM_SWIZZLE): GMMA::Layout_K_SW128_Atom<bfloat16_t>
```
The smem tiles `sA`/`sB` from `DecTcSmem` (megakernel:386-387) are reused as the
backing storage; wrap them with `make_tensor(make_smem_ptr(sA), SmemLayoutA{})`.

### 2.2 Per-k-step sequence (ascending k)
For each k-step (ascending), per ring slot:
1. **TMA load (if `SG_TUNED_GEMM_TMA`):** elected leader (`elect_one_sync`,
   warp_specialize.cuh:41) does `Mbarrier::arrive_expect_tx(tile_bytes)` then
   `SM90_TMA_LOAD::copy(desc_ptr, mbar, /*cache_hint*/0, smem_ptr, crd_mn, crd_k)`
   for A and B (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:95-117). `crd_k = k*16`. **No cluster needed**
   (cluster-size-1). Consumers `Mbarrier::try_wait(parity)` (warp_specialize.cuh:117).
   Else (`TMA==0`): keep the existing `cp_async_cg_16` staging (primitives.cuh) into
   the same `Layout_K_INTER` offsets — identical bytes.
2. **GMMA descriptors:** `make_gmma_desc<GMMA::Major::K>(smem_tensor)` (CuTe's
   `cute::GMMA::make_gmma_desc`, arch/mma_sm90_desc.hpp) builds the 64-bit smem
   descriptor from the `Layout_K_INTER` smem tensor — this REPLACES the hand
   `make_desc_A/B_kmajor`. Major::K ⇒ TransA=TransB=0 (matches tile_pipeline.cuh:335).
3. **MMA issue:** `wgs::wgmma_fence()` once before the chain (reuse the existing
   fence helper — it is the same `wgmma.fence.sync.aligned` PTX), then
   `Atom::fma(desc_a, desc_b, frag_c, /*scale_D=*/ (k==0 ? GMMA::ScaleOut::Zero :
   GMMA::ScaleOut::One))`. CuTe's atom `fma` emits the identical `wgmma.mma_async`
   PTX as `wgmma_issue_n128` ⇒ same hardware reduction. `wgmma_commit_group()` +
   `wgmma_wait_group<0>()` after (reuse the existing helpers, wgmma.cuh:385-403).
4. **M-atom interleave (kIL=2):** keep the project's structure — `frag_c` is an
   array of `kIL` accumulator fragments; issue the kIL atoms back-to-back per k into
   independent fragments sharing one B descriptor (mirrors issue_k,
   model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:750-762). CuTe fragment = `Atom`'s C-fragment type
   (`partition_fragment_C`); `N/2` fp32 regs — SAME register footprint as
   `WgmmaAccum<N>` ⇒ no new occupancy cost.

### 2.3 Pipelined ring (reuse the proven choreography)
Reuse `TilePipeline<N,Depth>` (tile_pipeline.cuh:142-189) — its `full`/`empty`
`Mbarrier` ring is single-CTA and cluster-free, so it composes with TMA directly
(the producer does `arrive_expect_tx` for the TMA bytes instead of cp.async). The
PIPE=2 producer/consumer split already exists in the decoder engine
(model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:860-987); swap its `cp_async_cg_16` producer body for
`SM90_TMA_LOAD::copy` + `arrive_expect_tx`, leaving the consumer (mbarrier wait +
MMA) unchanged. Default Depth=2 (double-buffer), `SG_TUNED_DEC_FWD_STAGES` up to 4.

### 2.4 CuTe-fragment epilogue
After `wgmma_wait_group<0>()`, store `frag_c`. To keep ONE validated source of truth,
**reuse `wgs::wgmma_frag_decode`** (wgmma.cuh:343-364) for the thread→(row,col) map
(the gate already validates it bit-for-bit) and emit through the same `out(row,col,v)`
accessor (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1100). CuTe's `partition_fragment_C` gives the
identical layout (both PTX §<ip>.3), but reusing the existing decode removes any
risk of a mismatched private decode. `if (col < n_real)` ragged guard preserved (1100).

---

## 3. KEEPING 1-CTA/SM + GridBarrier + ASCENDING-K DETERMINISM

- **1 CTA/SM:** no change to grid/block. Launch stays `<<<n_sms, 256>>>` (megakernel
  :1561), `__launch_bounds__(256)` (:673). The CuTe accumulator is the same `N/2`
  regs/thread; the addressing must stay lean (use hand-built `make_gmma_desc`, NOT a
  full `TiledMMA::partition` per k). The launcher's
  `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor ≥ 1` cert (:1540-1545) is the
  backstop: if CuTe regalloc drops occupancy < 1 CTA/SM, the launch REFUSES
  (`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`) and the operator keeps ENGINE=0. Add a build-time
  check (compile `-Xptxas -v`, inspect regs/spills) before flipping the flag default.
- **GridBarrier:** untouched. The CuTe GEMM runs ENTIRELY between `ctx.barrier()`
  calls (megakernel fwd/bwd/dW phases). TMA's mbarrier is a CTA-LOCAL smem barrier
  (different mechanism from the cross-CTA `GridBarrier`); they do not interact. No
  cluster ⇒ no `ClusterBarrier`, no cooperative launch — the hand `GridBarrier`
  (megakernel_common.cuh:147-255) scales unchanged.
- **Ascending-k determinism:** §2.2 keeps k ascending, k=0 overwrite (ScaleOut::Zero)
  / k>0 accumulate (ScaleOut::One). TMA reorders only WHEN a tile lands, never the
  issue order (same invariant the cp.async ring + PIPE=2 engine preserve,
  model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:876-886). No float atomics; one CTA owns the tile (dW
  split-K stays the deterministic ascending-chunk reduce, :96-101). Same atom + same
  no-swizzle smem bytes + same frag decode ⇒ **bit-identical to the hand path** ⇒
  `torch.equal` A/A/A (test:233) and fp64 rel-1e-4 (test:534) pass.

---

## 4. INCREMENTAL / GATED PATH (start with ONE GEMM)

Order of landing, each fully green before the next:

**Step 4.0 — Scaffolding, OFF.** Add `SG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE` (default 0),
`cute_gemm.cuh`, `cute_tma_desc.h`, the PersistentContext fields (nullable), include
`<cute/tensor.hpp>` in the TC TU. Build + run the FULL existing suite → must be
byte-identical (PTX diff vs baseline, like the project's existing OFF-vs-baseline
checks, model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:186). NOTHING calls the new engine yet.

**Step 4.1 — CuTe MMA atoms, cp.async staging, ONE GEMM.** Set
`SG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE=1, SG_TUNED_GEMM_TMA=0, SG_TUNED_GEMM_SWIZZLE=0`. Route ONLY
`dectc_gemm_fwd<128>` (model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1159) through `cute_gemm.cuh`'s
engine (CuTe `MMA_64x128x16_F32BF16BF16_SS::fma` + `make_gmma_desc` + reuse fence/
commit/wait + reuse cp.async staging + reuse `wgmma_frag_decode` epilogue). dX/dW
keep the hand engine. Gate:
  - `decoder_tc_selftest.cu` fwd micro-gate (per-orientation).
  - `test_decoder_tc.py::test_fwd_random` (rel≤2e-2 vs fp64), `test_fwd_identity`.
  - **Crucially `test_determinism_bitwise`** and the full-cell
    `test_tc_single_step_grad_parity` (still uses hand dX/dW; fwd now CuTe) — loss
    rel ≤ 1e-4. This proves the CuTe MMA atom is bit-equivalent to the hand wgmma.

**Step 4.2 — Add TMA load to fwd.** Flip `SG_TUNED_GEMM_TMA=1` for fwd only. Host
builds the fwd weight + acts descriptors (§1), uploads, sets `ctx.g_tma_desc`. The
fwd engine's producer uses `SM90_TMA_LOAD::copy` + `arrive_expect_tx`. Same gates.
Now the TMA path is silicon-proven on the simplest GEMM.

**Step 4.3 — Expand to dX.** Route `dectc_gemm_dx_f32<128>` (:1211) through the CuTe
engine; build dX descriptors over the C1-T transposed cache (`*_wT`). Gates:
`test_dx_random`, full-cell parity + determinism.

**Step 4.4 — dW (the big win).** Route `dectc_dw_run_tile<N>` /
`_splitk` (megakernel:924-930) through the CuTe engine WITH a TMA descriptor that
encodes the transpose (TMA can gather the transposed-strided dYᵀ·X operands that the
cp.async ring cannot — the current "out of scope" path,
model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:782-783). This removes the scalar gather. Gates:

**Step 4.5 — Swizzle perf phase.** Flip `SG_TUNED_GEMM_SWIZZLE=1`
(`Layout_K_SW128_Atom`). smem bytes now differ (swizzled), but the MMA math + fp32
order are identical (descriptor + TMA agree on the swizzle) ⇒ parity holds, A/A/A
holds (re-run all gates — determinism is per-fixed-config). Measure bank-conflict
elimination. This is the perf payoff the hand path flagged as TODO (wgmma.cuh:156-165).

**Step 4.6 — Generalize to vit / mamba.** Repeat 4.1-4.5 for
`model_stage_vit_tc.cuh` (uses the same `wgs::` engine, vit_tc:445-487) and
`model_stage_mamba_tc.cuh`. Each behind the same flags, each gated.

At every step: OFF (`SG_TUNED_GEMM_ENGINE=0`) MUST stay byte-identical (PTX diff);

  smem/occupancy unchanged at Depth=2.

  existing per-source nvcc flag rewrite, launcher.cu:15).

## 6. RISKS / OPEN ITEMS (be honest)

1. **CuTe register bloat.** `make_gmma_desc` + `Tensor` algebra can add address regs
   vs the hand path. MUST check `-Xptxas -v` (regs/spills) on the CuTe fwd TU before

   to know at compile. Mitigation: drive the atom `fma` with hand-built descriptors,
   avoid per-k `partition`.

   bf16 cache base / T change per B. Cache descriptors keyed on (base,rows,K) like the
   workspace cache (launcher.cu:55-71); rebuild on change. A stale descriptor = wrong

   the subtle part — validate dW LAST (Step 4.4) against `test_dw_identity_who_owns_
   what` (:211, the ownership/layout gate) before trusting it.
4. **Swizzle vs determinism.** Swizzle changes smem bytes; re-run A/A/A at the

   no-swizzle as the parity baseline.
5. **CUtensorMap availability.** Needs CUDA ≥ 12.0 driver + `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`.

   non-sm90 / old-CUDA build still compiles (ENGINE defaults OFF).
6. **No cluster, but TMA PTX says `shared::cluster`.** Confirmed valid at implicit
   cluster-size-1 (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:106). If a future sm wants multicast, that needs
   a real cluster — explicitly OUT of scope (1 CTA/SM is a hard constraint).
